meta.title: Richmond Events
meta.tagline: Everything worth showing up for in Richmond BC — dated events and standing weeklies, in one place.
meta.timezoneNote: All times are America/Vancouver (PDT until Nov 1, 2026, PST after).
meta.geographyNote: Richmond, BC, Canada (Metro Vancouver). Not Richmond VA, Richmond CA, Richmond Hill ON, or Richmond upon Thames UK.

events.title: Steveston Run Crew — Wednesday
events.summary: 5–10 km with all paces, rain or shine. The best night for a first-timer.
events.description:
A free community run of **5–10 km** that welcomes every pace and level, and goes ahead rain or shine.

Led by lululemon Richmond Centre ambassadors — coach Rachel and ambassador Dean. Of the crew's two weekly runs, Wednesday is the one to pick if you've never come before.

events.title: Steveston Run Crew — SRC Sundays
events.summary: The early Sunday session, out of Minoru Centre for Active Living.
events.description:
The Steveston Run Crew's second weekly run — an early start from the Minoru Centre for Active Living.

The crew posts the current week's route and pace groups to its Strava club, which is the most reliable place to check before heading out.

events.title: Richmond Olympic parkrun
events.summary: Free weekly timed 5K along the river. Register once, then just turn up.
events.description:
A **free weekly timed 5K** open to all abilities — run it, jog it, or walk it.

Registration is a **one-time** thing: sign up online, print or save your barcode, and after that you simply show up on any Saturday. Bring the barcode if you want a time recorded.

The course runs along the pathway beside River Road near Cambie Street.

venue.name: Pathway along River Road near Cambie Street
venue.address: River Rd & Cambie Rd, Richmond BC

events.title: Arc'teryx Run Club
events.summary: About 8 km at an easy pace through Richmond streets, from the Arc'teryx store.
events.description:
An easy-paced **~8 km** loop through Richmond streets, starting and finishing at the Arc'teryx store in Richmond Centre.

All running levels welcome. Led by run ambassador Tim Lee.

events.title: Kwantlen Farmers Market
events.summary: The only Richmond farmers market that runs into winter. Tuesdays through Dec 22.
events.description:
Local produce, gourmet foods, baked goods and handmade crafts, set up outside the Brighouse Library and Cultural Centre. Leashed pets are welcome.

Notable for being **the only Richmond farmers market operating into winter** — it runs every Tuesday until December 22, long after the Steveston market closes for the season.

events.title: Zodiac Bar Karaoke Night
events.summary: Free singing with a live backing band on Alexandra Road. Doors 6:30pm, start 7pm.
events.description:
Live-band karaoke — you sing, a band backs you. Billed as **"Sing for FREE"**, with light meals and affordable drinks available, and promotion in both English and Chinese.

Reserve by Instagram DM; group bookings are welcome.

> **Heads up:** Zodiac Bar has no confirmed website. Every detail here comes from a promotional flyer — confirm by phone or DM before you build a night around it.
events.caution: No official website confirmed. Details come from a promotional flyer — verify before relying on it.

events.title: Trues Club — Private Karaoke Rooms
events.summary: All-you-can-sing private rooms, weekend afternoons into the evening.
events.description:
**$25 per person** for an all-you-can-sing private room, or free karaoke out in the lounge with a **$20 minimum spend** per person. Food and drink combos run $20.

Room sizes: small seats 7–10, medium 12–18, large 20–25.

**Reservations are required.**

events.title: Lansdowne Food Garden — Free Gardening Workshops
events.summary: A free hour in the mall's food garden, Thursday afternoons through Oct 29.
events.description:
A free weekly gardening workshop in the Lansdowne Centre food garden.

The 2026 season runs **June 18 through October 29** — after that it stops for the winter.

events.title: Richmond Olympic Oval — Climbing wall & court drop-ins
events.unverifiedNote: Drop-in times vary by activity and season — see the Oval's schedule.
events.summary: Metro Vancouver's tallest climbing wall, six hardwood courts, two ice rinks and two tracks.
events.description:
The Oval's drop-in program covers a lot of ground:

- **Metro Vancouver's tallest climbing wall**
- Six hardwood sport courts for pickup basketball and volleyball
- Two ice rinks
- Two running tracks

Times shift by activity and season, so check the live schedule.

events.title: Lansdowne Free Outdoor Drive-In Movies
events.summary: Season ended Sep 2, 2026. Returns around summer 2027.
events.description:
Free outdoor movies in the Lansdowne Centre parking lot on Wednesday evenings — entry at 7:00 PM, film at sunset. First come, first served.

It isn't car-only: there's a **pedestrian viewing area at the front**, so bring a blanket, picnic mat or camping chairs. Bring a **portable FM radio** for the audio. The audience votes on the lineup.

**The 2026 season ended September 2.** Re-check around June 2027.

recurrence.text: Wednesdays in summer — 2026 season ended Sep 2

events.title: Steveston Farmers & Artisans Market — final date of the season
events.summary: Roughly 60 vendor booths at Garry Point Park — and the last one until spring.
events.description:

The market runs biweekly on Sundays through the season. **2026 dates were:** May 10 & 24, Jun 14 & 28, Jul 12 & 26, Aug 2, 16 & 30, and **Sep 13 — the final one.** It returns around May 2027.

events.title: Richmond Night Market — final day of the season
events.summary: The last night of the season — 500+ food offerings, zipline, ferris wheel, 7pm to midnight.
events.description:
The closing night of the 2026 Richmond Night Market, themed **"One World"**. The season ran April 24 through September 20.

On site: **500+ food offerings**, 100+ retail vendors, live performances, a **600-foot SkyRush zipline** and a ferris wheel.

**Practical notes:** some vendors are cash-only. Take the Canada Line to Bridgeport Station and walk — parking is limited.

> **Worth verifying:** 604now labelled this the market's *"Final Season"*, but Tourism Richmond's official page does not say that. Treat "last ever" as unconfirmed.
events.caution: The "final season" claim comes from a 604now post, not Tourism Richmond. Verify before treating Sep 20, 2026 as the permanent last day.

events.title: Steveston Christmas Craft Fair
events.flag: Bring cash — no ATM on site
events.summary: 165+ vendors of crafts, baking and jewellery. Bring cash — there is no ATM.
events.description:
The big one: **165+ vendors** (some sources say up to 125) selling homemade crafts, baking, jewellery and food items. There's a concession on site and a raffle.

**Bring cash — there is no ATM on site.**

Organized by the Steveston Community Society; vendor registration sold out in a single day.

> **Check the venue first.** Steveston Community Centre is under construction, so programs and this fair may be relocated to the Steveston Easthope Hub at 4320 Moncton St.
events.caution: Steveston Community Centre is under construction — the fair may be relocated to the Steveston Easthope Hub (4320 Moncton St). Confirm the venue.

A month of seasonal programming across Steveston Village — twinkling lights, seasonal displays, free family-friendly events, waterfront strolls, Santa visits, craft markets and puppy parades.

Includes **"Steveston Sips"**: village-wide festive drinks, appetizers and desserts at participating merchants.

Mostly free. The day-by-day calendar lists what's on each date.

Steveston Community Centre is under construction. Programs and the Christmas Craft Fair may move to the Steveston Easthope Hub (4320 Moncton St).

October is the thinnest month here — only Steveston Ghost Walks (Oct 3) and Secret Ingredients (Oct 14–17). The City of Richmond calendar publishes on a rolling ~30/90-day window, so re-scrape it in early October.
